**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination / Technical and Vocational Education Examination. Subject: Religious Studies (code 0785), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Paper 2: The Old Testament/Jewish Bible and World Faiths. Duration: three hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR questions chosen from any ONE SECTION ONLY. All questions carry equal marks (25 marks each).

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Sections of the paper: 1.0 The Old Testament/Jewish Bible, Section 1.1 The Patriarchs to David (questions 1 to 6); Section 5.3 Islam (questions 7 to 12); Section 5.5 African Traditional Religious Beliefs and Practices (questions 13 to 18).

Neutralité : les croyances sont présentées comme celles des musulmans (« Muslims believe », « according to Islamic tradition ») ; aucun numéro de sourate ni de hadith n'est cité.

Règle de choix : le sujet impose « Answer FOUR questions chosen from any ONE SECTION ONLY ». Cette règle (4 questions d'UNE SEULE section) n'est pas exprimable avec `parmi` (un seul groupe) ni `ou` (sous-questions) : `regles_choix` reste vide dans tous les fichiers et la consigne complète est recopiée dans `introduction_markdown`.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées de mémoire, sans accès à une source ; les références sont limitées à des passages et faits bien établis, les autres points sont formulés prudemment (« according to Islamic tradition », « Muslims believe »). À faire relire par un spécialiste des études religieuses avant mise en avant.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Show how prayers can be 'the master key' in the religion of the Muslims

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Prayer (salat) is the second pillar of Islam, performed five times a day. A key opens a door; a master key opens many. To show how prayer can be "the master key" for Muslims is to show how it opens the way to many blessings: closeness to God, forgiveness, discipline, community and success in this life and the next. Islamic tradition itself describes prayer as the key to Paradise.

**1. It opens the way to God.** The five daily prayers (Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha) are a direct meeting between the worshipper and God. There is no priest between them. Muslims believe that when they pray, they stand before the Lord, so prayer is the key to closeness (qurb) to God.

**2. It is the foundation of the other acts of faith.** After the declaration of faith (shahadah), prayer is the first practical duty. Muslims hold that it comes first in the account on the Day of Judgement, and that if it is sound the rest of one's deeds will be judged well. It is thus the key to the acceptance of other acts of worship.

**3. It brings forgiveness and spiritual cleansing.** The Prophet compared the five prayers to a river flowing by one's door in which a person bathes five times a day, leaving no dirt. The preparation, including ablution (wudu), gives physical and spiritual purity, and prayer is a regular occasion for asking forgiveness.

**4. It restrains from evil and shapes character.** The Qur'an says that prayer keeps a person away from shameful and unjust deeds. Regular prayer builds discipline, honesty, humility and patience. Its postures, especially prostration (sujud), express submission to God and break pride.

**5. It structures time and daily life.** The prayer times divide the day, reminding believers of God from dawn to night. The sense of order and of using time well passes into work, family and business.

**6. It builds community and equality.** In congregational prayer, and especially the Friday prayer (jumu'ah) and the festival prayers, Muslims stand shoulder to shoulder, rich and poor, all facing the same direction (the Ka'bah in Makkah). This builds unity, equality and brotherhood, and opens a way to solidarity and mutual help in the community.

**7. It brings peace of mind and a way of seeking help.** The Qur'an urges believers to seek help through patience and prayer. Muslims turn to prayer in difficulties, fear, grief and in decisions (including the special prayer of guidance, istikharah), finding calm and strength.

**8. It is a key to Paradise.** According to a well-known saying attributed to the Prophet, the key to Paradise is prayer, and the key to prayer is purification. Muslims believe that those who keep their prayers regularly have hope of reward in the hereafter.

**Qualification.** Prayer is not the only key: faith, zakat, fasting, pilgrimage and good conduct are also required, and Muslims stress that prayer must be accompanied by sincerity and good behaviour towards others.

**Conclusion.** Prayer is "the master key" in Islam because it opens the way to God, supports every other religious duty, cleanses the believer, shapes character, organises daily life, unites the community and, Muslims hope, leads to Paradise.
